signals.title: DIGIFLOAT digital twin for WindFloat Atlantic
signals.connectionToFowt: ARPA-E identifies DIGIFLOAT as digital twin software tailored to floating offshore wind and tied to the WindFloat Atlantic floating wind project.
signals.shortDescription: Principle Power led an ATLANTIS project to develop, validate and operate a real-time digital twin representation of WindFloat Atlantic.
signals.whyItMatters: The signal is tied to full-scale floating platforms and metocean prediction, so it is directly relevant to floating wind design and operations rather than generic asset software.

signals.title: NextWind applies industrial DataOps to offshore wind digital twins
signals.connectionToFowt: The California Energy Commission report frames NextWind around offshore wind assets, California offshore wind planning goals and floating wind monitoring challenges.
signals.shortDescription: Aker Offshore Wind, Cognite and H. T. Harvey & Associates developed a digital twin architecture for offshore wind asset monitoring and environmental interaction use cases.
signals.whyItMatters: It links industrial data infrastructure with offshore wind integrity management, condition monitoring and environmental monitoring needs expected for floating projects.

signals.title: ACE-FWICC uses scientific machine learning for floating wind systems
signals.connectionToFowt: PNNL describes ACE-FWICC as an Energy Earthshot Research Center focused on floating offshore wind design, control and grid integration using scientific machine learning.
signals.shortDescription: The center connects metocean, turbine, farm and grid models to study floating offshore wind in a changing climate.
signals.whyItMatters: The work targets engineering questions that affect floating wind siting, control, lifetime estimation and grid integration, with machine learning used as an engineering tool.

signals.title: DTWO develops federated digital twins for offshore wind
signals.connectionToFowt: CORDIS describes DTWO as a Horizon Europe project for offshore wind digital twins covering offshore wind production systems, including bottom-fixed and floating wind turbines and farms.
signals.shortDescription: DTWO is building a federated digital twin architecture that integrates simulation assets and real-time data without centralising commercially sensitive data.
signals.whyItMatters: The federated model matters because offshore wind digitalisation often needs shared models while protecting project and operator data.

signals.title: ECMWF advances DTWO weather, wake and grid modules
signals.connectionToFowt: ECMWF reports that DTWO modules address offshore wind siting, wake effects, turbine monitoring, grid connectivity and energy-market integration.
signals.shortDescription: ECMWF described progress on DTWO plugins for extreme events and wind-farm parameterisation within the Destination Earth digital twin environment.
signals.whyItMatters: Weather, wave and wake modelling are core constraints for offshore wind operations, maintenance access and grid-relevant production forecasting.

signals.title: DIONYSOS tested hybrid digital monitoring on floating turbines
signals.connectionToFowt: France Energies Marines states that DIONYSOS developed and tested in-service fatigue monitoring tools on Zefyros and DemoSATH floating offshore wind turbines.
signals.shortDescription: The project combined sensors, numerical simulations and software coupling to analyse operating floating wind turbine behaviour and anomalies.
signals.whyItMatters: It is a field-tested floating wind monitoring signal, with digital methods tied to fatigue, reliability and anomaly categorisation.

signals.title: SUBSEE 4D built digital twin tools for floating wind moorings
signals.connectionToFowt: France Energies Marines describes SUBSEE 4D as a digital twin project to facilitate the operation of floating wind farms and monitor mooring lines.
signals.shortDescription: The project developed in-service monitoring software, numerical models, sensor strategy and machine-learning tools for anomaly prediction and classification.
signals.whyItMatters: Floating wind moorings are a project-critical subsystem, and this signal connects digital twin methods to in-service reliability rather than generic analytics.

signals.title: ATLANTIS tested autonomous robots at WindFloat Atlantic
signals.connectionToFowt: INESC TEC states that the ATLANTIS project tested autonomous vehicles for inspection and monitoring at the WindFloat Atlantic floating offshore wind farm.
signals.shortDescription: Autonomous surface, underwater and aerial robotic technologies were demonstrated for visual and thermographic inspection around floating wind structures.
signals.whyItMatters: Robotic inspection is directly relevant to offshore access, safety and O&M cost for floating wind farms where manual inspection is difficult.

signals.title: SaturnX develops autonomous satcom-enabled drone inspection
signals.connectionToFowt: ESA Space Solutions describes SaturnX as an autonomous, remotely operated drone service for offshore wind farm inspection using satcom and an offshore launch/recovery/recharge platform.
signals.shortDescription: The project combines offshore drone bases, BVLOS satellite communication, sensors and AI-supported inspection workflows for wind turbine towers, blades and nacelles.
signals.whyItMatters: It targets inspection logistics and data capture for offshore wind O&M, with autonomy and communications treated as operational constraints.

signals.title: AIRU-WRF applies AI to offshore wind forecasting and grid integration
signals.connectionToFowt: NOWRDC describes AIRU-WRF as an AI-powered offshore wind forecasting project for U.S. Mid-Atlantic and Northeastern offshore wind energy areas and grid integration.
signals.shortDescription: Rutgers University is developing and demonstrating physics-guided AI forecasting for offshore wind resource and power-output prediction.
signals.whyItMatters: Forecast accuracy affects offshore wind production decisions, market operations and grid integration, making this an energy-system signal rather than generic AI forecasting.
organizations: National Offshore Wind Research and Development Consortium

signals.title: Computer vision and AI for offshore wind blade monitoring
signals.connectionToFowt: NOWRDC identifies the project as offshore wind turbine blade monitoring using drone-based inspection, computer vision and AI.
signals.shortDescription: The University of Massachusetts Lowell project develops UAV and AI methods to identify location and severity of offshore wind blade damage.
signals.whyItMatters: Blade inspection frequency, service interruption and scarce inspector capacity are practical O&M constraints for offshore wind operators.
organizations: National Offshore Wind Research and Development Consortium

signals.title: E-PROA integrates AI digital twin and O&M vessel concepts
signals.connectionToFowt: The E-PROA project describes an integrated digital platform for operation and maintenance of floating wind farms, including an AI predictive digital twin.
signals.shortDescription: The project combines predictive AI-based digital twin work with floating wind O&M strategy, an eco-SOV concept and underwater cable and anchoring inspection tooling.
signals.whyItMatters: It connects digital engineering to practical floating wind O&M architecture, including vessels, cables, anchors and decision support.

signals.title: FlexiWind models virtual offshore wind farms for flexible operation
signals.connectionToFowt: Fraunhofer IWES describes FlexiWind as using a digital twin of a real offshore wind farm to develop data-driven flexible operation for grid support, load optimisation and predictive maintenance.
signals.shortDescription: The project develops and validates a digital twin for virtual offshore wind farm operation and control strategy testing.
signals.whyItMatters: Flexible wind farm operation sits between turbine loads, maintenance, electricity output and grid support, making it a digital engineering and power-system signal.

signals.title: IEA frames AI data-centre demand as an energy-system issue
signals.connectionToFowt: The IEA Energy and AI report treats data-centre electricity demand as a power-system issue and identifies renewables, including wind, as part of current and future supply.
signals.shortDescription: The report assesses how AI-related data-centre demand changes electricity supply requirements and the role of renewables in meeting that demand.
signals.whyItMatters: For FOWT Digest this belongs only as grid and renewable-energy infrastructure context: compute demand can affect clean-power procurement and grid planning, but it is not generic AI news.
